boundary: Old lake-bed clays (Lake Texcoco/Xochimilco-Chalco: Centro, Neza, the airport, Tláhuac, Valle de Chalco), sinking because groundwater is pumped out, vs. stable volcanic ground: the Sierra de Santa Catarina and Cerro de la Estrella in the east, the Chapultepec/Lomas hills in the west, and the Xitle lava of the Pedregal (Ciudad Universitaria) in the south. Values are NISAR cumulative LOS motion, 2025-10-30 to 2026-10-13. The fastest pixels are about -45 cm in Valle de Chalco/Tláhuac (19.26-19.27N, 98.97-99.05W) and -30 to -34 cm near the old Texcoco lakebed by Neza/the airport (19.44N, 99.00-99.03W). Hills read +2 to +3 cm, which is likely a reference offset, i.e. effectively stable.

items.title: A kilometre-long crack runs under homes on the Tláhuac / Valle de Chalco line
items.place: Calle Luciano Navarrete x Calle El Pípila, Santa Catarina Yecahuízotl, Tláhuac, CDMX; continuing under Calle Rafael Núñez, Valle de Chalco (Edomex)
items.what_it_shows: News photo and story. A crack about 1.5 m wide crosses Eje 10 Sur at a petrol station and reaches the corner of Luciano Navarrete and El Pípila, through the colonias San Miguel, Barrio de la Concepción and Santa Catarina. Cars slow to cross it and houses tilt. In Valle de Chalco, Lourdes Baltazar's house on Calle Rafael Núñez lost a wall in the 2017 quake; her patio sank until the family 'built steps', and her neighbour has had no water for six months because the pipe broke.
items.notes: Both streets were geocoded with Nominatim: Calle Luciano Navarrete is at 19.3093,-98.9649 and Calle El Pípila at 19.3125,-98.9659, both in Guadalupe Yecahuizotl, Santa Catarina, Tláhuac. The intersection was not geocoded directly, so ±300 m. The story predates NISAR by four years. The image is the article's og:image, a link only.

items.title: Sierra de Santa Catarina: the volcanic ridge that doesn't sink
items.place: Sierra de Santa Catarina (volcanoes Yuhualixqui, Xaltepec, Tetecón, Tecuauhtzin, Guadalupe, La Caldera), Iztapalapa/Tláhuac
items.what_it_shows: Photo: the line of volcanic cones of the Sierra de Santa Catarina, taken from the summit of Cerro de la Estrella, looking SE over the Iztapalapa lowland (2005). An alternative image, 'Volcan Yuhualixqui visto desde San Pedro Tláhuac' (ProtoplasmaKid, CC BY-SA 4.0, 2022, GPS 19.269241,-99.005417), looks north at the same ridge from the sinking Tláhuac lake-bed. NISAR reads -13.2 cm at that camera position (window -16.5 to -12.4). One frame, both sides of the boundary.
items.notes: Coordinates are from the es.wikipedia 'Sierra de Santa Catarina' article and are a ridge centroid. es.wikipedia confirms it is a range of monogenetic volcanoes. Alt image direct URL: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/16/Volcan_Yuhualixqui_visto_desde_San_Pedro_Tl%C3%A1huac.jpg (page https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Volcan_Yuhualixqui_visto_desde_San_Pedro_Tl%C3%A1huac.jpg). The Cerro de la Estrella summit (19.3436,-99.09) reads +3.3 cm and is also stable.

items.title: Templo de la Santísima Trinidad: a church now below street level
items.place: Templo de la Santísima Trinidad, Centro Histórico (Calle Santísima / Emiliano Zapata), CDMX
items.what_it_shows: 1986 photo captioned 'The level of the building is lower than the recent environment, due to ground subsidence': the church floor sits below the surrounding pavement.
items.notes: The 1986 file has no GPS. The coordinate comes from ProtoplasmaKid's 2012 Commons photos of the same church (File:Templo_de_la_Santísima_Trinidad.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0, GPS 19.433164,-99.126650), which also make a good modern image. Do not confuse it with the Methodist 'Templo de la Santísima Trinidad' on Gante (19.4333,-99.1399), which Nominatim returns first. Same photographer, same theme: 'Ciudad de México, edificios 1986 02.jpg' (La Profesa, also below street level) and 'calles y plazas 1986 07.jpg' (Loreto church tilted).

items.title: The Metropolitan Cathedral, sinking unevenly into the lake-bed
items.what_it_shows: The cathedral's facade and bell towers from the Zócalo (2024). English Wikipedia: 'The cathedral, along with the rest of the city, has been sinking into the lakebed from the day it was built'. In the late 20th century parts of the complex were sinking at different rates and the bell towers were tilting dangerously. Underpinning work 'corrected the tilting towers and ensured that the cathedral will sink uniformly'. It was placed on the World Monuments Fund's 100 Most Endangered Sites list.
items.credit: ProtoplasmaKid, via Wikimedia Commons; text: en.wikipedia 'Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral'
items.notes: The item coordinate is the building (en.wikipedia). The photo GPS is 19.432907,-99.133108, the camera position in the Zócalo. Palacio de Bellas Artes (19.4353,-99.1414) reads -4.2 cm, but I did not find a fetched page confirming its sinking.

items.title: Ángel de la Independencia: 14 steps added as the ground fell away
items.place: Monumento a la Independencia, Paseo de la Reforma x Florencia, CDMX
items.what_it_shows: The column and its stepped base at night (2013). English Wikipedia: 'Originally, nine steps led to the base, but due to land subsidence, an ongoing problem in Mexico City, fourteen more steps have been added.'
items.credit: Diego Delso, via Wikimedia Commons; text: en.wikipedia 'Angel of Independence'
items.notes: The coordinate is the photo's GPS, which matches Wikipedia's 19.4270,-99.1677 to about 50 m. Why the column stays put while the street drops (its deep foundation) is often said but was not verified on a fetched page, so I left it out. A closer view of the base: File:BaseAngelInd.JPG (Thelmadatter, CC BY-SA 3.0, 2010).

items.title: Ciudad Universitaria on the Pedregal lava: the stable south
items.place: Torre de Rectoría, Ciudad Universitaria (UNAM), Coyoacán, CDMX
items.what_it_shows: Mario Pani's Rectoría tower (2011). es.wikipedia: the Pedregal de San Ángel site chosen in 1943 'es producto de erupciones volcánicas, principalmente del volcán Xitle', i.e. solid lava, not lake clay.
items.credit: ProtoplasmaKid, via Wikimedia Commons; text: es.wikipedia 'Ciudad Universitaria (UNAM)'
items.notes: The photo GPS is 19.332769,-99.188325; es.wikipedia puts the Torre de Rectoría at 19.331953,-99.18823, about 90 m away. The western hills could be shown with File:Castillo_de_Chapultepec_de_día.jpg (Lasibris, CC BY 4.0, no GPS; castle at 19.42056,-99.18167, +1.6 cm).
